guidance.title: Attend your Blue Card appointment with the originals
guidance.description:
Cologne reviews your online application and sends you an appointment invitation if it can issue the Blue Card.
Bring the originals of the documents listed below. In individual cases the office may ask for further documents.

instructions.body: First issue €100, renewal €93. Turkish nationals with association rights pay €22.80 up to 24 years of age, €37 from 24 years.
instructions.title: Pay the fee at the appointment

instructions.body: In the first 12 months you must report every change of employer through Cologne's contact form, with the termination of the old job and the new contract. You need no permission for the change and can start immediately, but the office can suspend the change for 30 days and refuse it if the Blue Card conditions are not met.
instructions.title: Know the job-change rule for your first 12 months

guidance.title: Prepare the evidence for your first Blue Card application
guidance.description:
If you hold a national D visa and plan to apply for an EU Blue Card, get your evidence ready and apply before your visa expires. If you do, your visa is treated as still valid after it expires, until the Ausländerbehörde (foreigners' office) decides (§81 AufenthG).

Cologne asks for these with every application:
- a valid passport or passport substitute
- a biometric passport photo no older than three months
- the employment contract or a binding job offer
- if you have it, the Federal Employment Agency's pre-approval; otherwise the completed form "Erklärung zum Beschäftigungsverhältnis" (employment declaration form)
- if you rent, the rental contract and a bank statement showing the current rent payment
- if you own your home, a land-register extract and proof of the monthly costs for interest, repayments and running costs
- proof of full health insurance if you are not statutorily insured

For a first application, Cologne also needs proof of one of these qualifications:
- a university degree certificate
  - foreign degree: certified German or English translation, plus an anabin extract or a certificate evaluation from the Zentralstelle für ausländisches Bildungswesen (ZAB, the German office that evaluates foreign degrees; anabin is its online database)
- a certificate of a tertiary education programme and recognition of that qualification
- for IT specialists without a formal qualification, proof of at least three years' IT work experience within the last seven years and a CV

For regulated professions, also bring your licence to practise.
If your entry required a visa, bring your visa for qualified employment.
In individual cases Cologne may ask for further documents.

The job offer must cover at least six months and the statutory Blue Card conditions still have to be checked. This is preparation, not a prediction that the application will be approved.

guidance.title: File your annual income tax return (Einkommensteuererklärung)
guidance.description:
As an employee, wage tax is deducted from your salary. A tax return is
mandatory in the cases listed in §46 EStG — for example if you were paid by
several employers at the same time — and if the tax office asks you to.
If none of those cases applies, you can still file a return to have the
wage tax already withheld credited against your income tax. A time limit
applies to that (see the steps). If you are required to file and do it
yourself, the return is due seven months after the end of the calendar
year; a different deadline applies when a tax adviser prepares it.

instructions.body: Your employer must hand you a printout of your electronic wage tax certificate or make it available electronically. It summarises the wage and wage tax of the year.
instructions.title: Collect your Lohnsteuerbescheinigung

instructions.body: Read the cases listed in §46 EStG, or ask your tax office or a tax adviser. You must also file if the tax office asks you to. If you are not required to file, filing is your choice. If you file voluntarily, a time limit of four years applies (§169 AO). Ask your tax office when it ends for a given year. Once it has ended, the tax office can no longer assess your tax, so the wage tax withheld can no longer be credited against your income tax.
instructions.title: Check whether you must file

guidance.title: Check and prepare your address registration (Anmeldung)
guidance.description:
Registration normally follows moving into a dwelling, with a two-week
period under §17 BMG. Temporary stays and other situations can fall under
exceptions in §27 BMG. Check the applicable procedure with the registration
authority if your circumstances are unclear. Employment or a permanent
residence title does not by itself answer this question.
This card helps you prepare; it does not decide that an exception is absent.
Any displayed preparation target uses your move-in date, not your arrival
date or an appointment, and is not a confirmed personal legal deadline.

instructions.body: Open the city page for online eligibility, attendance and any additional family or foreign civil-status documents. Confirm unclear cases with the authority.
instructions.title: Check the procedure and documents for your move

instructions.body: If confirmation is refused or not provided in time, notify the registration authority without delay as required by §19(2) BMG. Do not assume that missing proof or a later appointment extends a deadline.
instructions.title: Get the move-in confirmation

instructions.body: Keep the confirmation after registration; completing this preparation card does not mean the authority has registered you.

guidance.title: Confirm health insurance cover for your stay
guidance.description:
Confirm which cover applies to your stay and when it starts. Statutory and
private insurance have different entry conditions and exceptions; this card
does not decide which system you qualify for. Check any period between
arrival and the start of employment with your insurer and, where relevant,
the German mission abroad. Do not assume you have an uninsured grace period.

instructions.body: Explain your work or study situation, existing cover and planned dates. Ask the insurer which cover and documents apply; do not wait for address registration before making this enquiry.

instructions.body: Check the start date and any gap between policies. Keep the insurer's confirmation. Expadu does not approve an insurer or confirm legal sufficiency of your cover.

guidance.title: A child born in Germany: check citizenship first
guidance.description:
Check first whether your child is German by birth.
A child of foreign parents born in Germany becomes German if, at the birth, one parent
has lived here lawfully for five years and also either
holds an unlimited right of residence (a permanent right to stay)
or is an EU citizen with free movement rights.
Parents from an EEA country or Switzerland: ask the city how this applies to you.
The city checks this automatically, without you applying;
the check takes a few weeks, and you are told without asking if your child is German.
Your child usually also has your citizenship: check with your home consulate and register the child there too.

If your child is not German, the parents' permits at the birth decide what happens.
When both parents or the parent with sole custody hold a residence permit, a Niederlassungserlaubnis or a Daueraufenthalt-EU,
the child gets its own residence permit automatically, without applying.
Otherwise, apply within six months of the birth, even if only one parent holds a permit;
the office can then grant it automatically, but don't wait for that.
If a parent holds a visa or may stay visa-free at the birth, the child's stay counts as allowed only until the visa or visa-free stay ends,
so apply before then, even if that is sooner.
Ask the Ausländerbehörde which documents to bring, and start the child's passport at your consulate early.
The office may give you a Fiktionsbescheinigung, a paper showing what the application means for the child's stay.

The birth must be reported to the Standesamt within one week;
if your child is born in a Cologne hospital, the hospital handles this with the Standesamt.
Registering the birth is free.
Your child's tax ID arrives automatically by post from the Bundeszentralamt für Steuern;
you need it to apply for Kindergeld.
Tell your Krankenkasse about the birth.
If you are not married to each other, recognition of paternity is needed:
the father can recognise paternity even before the birth,
the mother must consent, and it is free of charge at the Standesamt or the Bezirksjugendamt.

guidance.title: Find or recover your Steuer-ID (tax identification number)
guidance.description:
Your tax identification number stays the same for life, including after a
move or marriage. Check an existing income tax assessment or wage tax
certificate before requesting it again. If you do not have it, follow the
BZSt procedure. This preparation task is not a delivery promise or deadline.

instructions.body: Check your income tax assessment or wage tax certificate. Do not enter the number in Expadu.
instructions.title: Look for an existing number

instructions.body: BZSt provides a recovery procedure for a lost number. For first registration, its instructions say to request the number if no letter has arrived within three months. It is not disclosed by phone or email.
instructions.title: Use the official recovery instructions if needed

guidance.title: Church tax: how church membership affects your tax
guidance.description:
Church tax is calculated from your income tax.
It follows your legal membership of a religious community that levies tax.
The registration office reports this membership, and any change to it, to the Federal Central Tax Office.
If you are employed, your employer withholds church tax together with the income tax taken from your salary (wage tax).
Once a change such as joining or leaving a church is in the registration register, it is taken into account automatically for wage tax.
No employer? If you pay income tax prepayments, church tax prepayments are due at the same time.

guidance.title: German citizenship
guidance.description:
German citizenship is usually after five years of lawful residence in Germany,
with German at level B1 (or a German school, study or vocational qualification)
and proof of knowledge of the legal and social order, for example a passed
naturalisation test (Einbürgerungstest). The fee is €255. Other conditions, such
as your residence title and secured livelihood, also apply.

guidance.title: Other permit types: where to look
guidance.description:
Some paths we don't model in full. Here is where the law puts them.
Vocational training in a company (§16a) has its own residence permit for
training. Researchers (§18d) need a hosting agreement or contract with a research
institution; intra-corporate transfers (§19) use the ICT Card for a temporary
posting within the company group. Language courses (§16f) and searching for a
training place (§17) have their own residence permits. Long-term residents of
another EU country (§38a) who hold that status there can get a residence permit
if they want to stay in Germany for more than 90 days. Ask the Ausländeramt which
route applies to you.

legal_sources.label: §17 AufenthG — Suche eines Ausbildungs- oder Studienplatzes

guidance.title: New passport? Transfer your permit (Übertrag)
guidance.description:
Your residence title stays valid when you get a new national passport. Carry
both the old and the new passport if you kept the old one. If the old passport
number is printed on your residence title, contact the Ausländeramt through its
contact form and it will tell you the next steps; if it is not printed there,
you do not need to do anything. Settlement permit holders whose card shows the
passport number book an appointment at their Bezirksausländeramt and bring your
old passport, your new passport and a digital biometric photo. Also worth
knowing: a residence title generally expires if you leave Germany for a reason
that is not temporary, or if you stay abroad for longer than six months without
a longer period set by the Ausländerbehörde. Some exceptions apply, so ask
before planning long stays away.

Stadt Köln · Antworten auf Fragen zum Aufenthalt

guidance.definition_title: Moving your permit to a new passport

guidance.title: Fiktionsbescheinigung: what that bridging paper really permits
guidance.description:
While a permit application is processing you may get a Fiktionsbescheinigung —
and what it allows depends on which of its two forms you hold. The continuation
form (§81 Abs. 4) keeps your current permit in force until the decision: you may
keep working if your permit allowed it, and you may travel and return while it is
valid. The form for a first application without a visa (§81 Abs. 3) does not
allow work, and you may not leave Germany and re-enter on it. Check which form
yours is before booking any flight.

guidance.title: The long game: permanent residency
guidance.description:
Germany rewards staying. A Niederlassungserlaubnis (permanent residency) is
usually after holding a residence permit for five years, with secured
livelihood, at least 60 months of pension contributions (in a marriage, the
contributions of one spouse can count for both), German at level B1, basic
knowledge of the legal and social order (usually shown with the "Leben in
Deutschland" test) and sufficient housing for your household. The Cologne fee is
€113. Faster routes exist: three years on a skilled-worker permit (two years with
a German degree or vocational training) under §18c; 27 months on a Blue Card, or
21 months with sufficient German; three years for family members of Germans (§28). The EU
variant (Daueraufenthalt-EU, §9a) also generally needs five years. When a renewal
comes due, check whether you already meet these conditions.

guidance.title: Inviting family or friends to visit? Verpflichtungserklärung
guidance.description:
If you invite visa-required family or friends to visit, they can use a
Verpflichtungserklärung to show the German embassy or consulate that their costs
are covered. You commit to covering public costs of their stay, for five years
from their entry.

Who can sign: You need your main residence in Cologne and a regular income
that could be seized if you don't pay; your net income must be above the amount
protected from seizure (Pfändungsfreigrenze). If you receive Bürgergeld, social
assistance (Sozialhilfe), Wohngeld or Lastenzuschuss (a housing-cost subsidy for
homeowners), you cannot invite visa-required guests.

If your guest stays more than 90 days and you hold a fixed-term residence permit,
your permit must stay valid longer than your guest's stay and your commitment.

How to file: at the Ausländeramt, at least three months before their visa
appointment, by post, online contact form, or in person on Tuesday and Thursday
mornings. The fee is €29 per declaration and is charged even if your income is
not sufficient. The embassy usually recognises it for up to six months after issue.

What to bring:
- Everyone (employees, self-employed people and freelancers): the application
  form and a valid ID card, travel document (Reiseausweis) or a residence permit
  valid for at least six months.
- Employees also: payslips for the last three months and a bank statement for
  the last full month showing the salary.
- Self-employed people also, instead of payslips: a current Steuerberater
  certificate of your net monthly income for the last three months, or your last
  tax assessment. Plus a bank statement for the last full month.
- Freelancers also: bank statements for the last three months, plus the same
  Steuerberater certificate or your last tax assessment.

guidance.title: Foreign professional qualification? Get it recognized
guidance.description:
Some professions are regulated: you may only work in them after a state approval procedure and recognition of your qualification.
In Germany, jobs in health and education are among the regulated ones, for example doctor, nurse or nursery teacher.
In other jobs you need no formal recognition to work, but having your qualifications assessed can still help employers judge them. This is only about doing the job itself: if you need a residence permit, check that permit's card for what it asks of your qualification.
Your nationality does not matter for the procedure.
You apply to the office responsible for your profession. To find out whether your job is regulated and which office that is, use the portal www.anerkennung-in-deutschland.de or call the "Working and Living in Germany" hotline (Hotline Arbeiten und Leben in Deutschland) on +49 30-1815-1111.
Doctors need a licence to practise (Approbation); the authority of the federal state where you want to work as a doctor decides on it.
The procedure costs fees, set by the responsible office; once all documents are complete, it should as a rule take no longer than three months.
Have a university degree? The database of the education ministers' conference (link below) gives a good overview of the equivalence of foreign academic degrees.
